subject: POC trial: model selection & evaluation plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC trial: model selection & evaluation plan - post-call recap

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for the productive discovery call today. Quick recap of what we heard and a proposed plan for the POC/trial: 

Key success criteria (as we understood):
- Intent classification accuracy >= 92% on your labeled test set
- Entity extraction / slot-filling F1 >= 90%
- Response relevance / hallucination rate < 2% on business-critical prompts
- Latency p95 < 300ms for single-request flows (your SLA target)
- Cost target: aim to keep inference cost under $X per 1k tokens for production scale (we'll tighten this after measurements)

Multilingual requirement: Spanish and Portuguese support for both understanding and generation. We discussed whether to use a native multilingual model vs. translation pipeline — we'll evaluate both during the POC.

Proposed model plan for the trial:
- Primary candidate: Llama-2-Chat-13B (4-bit quantized) — good balance of latency, cost, and instruction-following for English-first flows
- Multilingual option: BloomZ / multilingual fine-tuned variant for native Spanish/Portuguese testing (run A/B with primary)
- Fallback: Mistral-instruct-7B quantized (fast, lower cost) for degraded capacity / burst mode; also consider a smaller 3rd-party 7B quantized model for offline/failover
- Option B for multilingual: translation step (Spanish->English) + primary model -> translate back (if native multilingual model underperforms)

Evaluation plan (2-week POC):
- Week 0 (pre-kickoff): exchange sample prompts, labels, and a 1000-row test set from Acme (we'll keep this private)
- Week 1 (integration): integrate Redwood SDK endpoint, baseline runs with primary & multilingual candidates, capture latency/cost metrics and generate outputs for evaluation
- Week 2 (tuning & evaluation): run tuned runs, compute metrics (accuracy, F1, hallucination checks), QA with your SMEs, and produce final recommendation + cost projection

Ownership / roles:
- Ben Carter (AE) — commercial/SLAs/contract coordination
- Aditya Rao (SE) — technical lead, integration, model configuration, eval harness
- Laura Bennett (CS) — success criteria alignment and rollout planning
- Acme stakeholders: Sofia Martinez (POC owner), Carlos Ruiz (technical decision-maker)

Next steps:
1) Sofia to confirm dataset share and privacy constraints (S3 link or upload to shared Drive).
2) We'll circulate a short POC statement of work (attachment) and a trial MSA/TOU (if needed).
3) Proposed kickoff: Mon, Oct 4 at 11:00 AM PT — confirm availability.

I've attached a draft POC plan and a simple open-model comparison table to get us started.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_poc_plan_v1.pdf (POC plan), open-model-comparison.csv (high-level model tradeoffs)

Thanks Ben — this looks great and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from my side:

- Multilingual: Spanish and Portuguese are must-haves. Ideally the model should handle regional variants (LatAm Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese). If the native multilingual models fall short, the translation pipeline is acceptable but we prefer native support if possible.
- Data retention / compliance: we need details on data retention, customer-managed KMS, and SOC2 artifacts for the trial. I attached our internal POC requirements spreadsheet for your reference.
- Offline / fallback mode: for certain customer touchpoints we may need a smaller on-prem or edge-fallback model — can you outline options for that?

Our legal/ procurement team will also want a short statement of work and an accounting of expected traffic for sizing. Carlos will be looped in for technical validation.

Available for kickoff Oct 4 at 11am PT.

— Sofia
Sofia Martinez
Head of Product, Acme Analytics

Thanks Sofia — great notes. Quick replies inline: 

- Regional variants: we'll include targeted prompts for LatAm Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese in the test set. If native multilingual models underperform we'll fallback to the translation pipeline as discussed.
- Data retention & compliance: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS and configurable retention policies (we can retain tokens for 0/7/30/90 days depending on your needs). We'll also provide SOC 2 artifacts and an export of audit logs for the trial; attaching a short SOC2 summary now.
- Offline/fallback: options include a quantized 7B model deployed to a small Dedicated pool or an on-prem package (requires additional setup). We'll outline the cost and ops tradeoffs in the SOW.

I'll have Aditya produce a recommended model configuration matrix and a lightweight eval harness we can run against your sample set.

Confirming kickoff Mon, Oct 4 at 11:00 AM PT — we'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Ben

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: POC trial: model selection & evaluation plan - technical recommendations

Hi all — following up with a technical recommendation for the POC model matrix and evaluation signals. High level: we'll run an A/B across two approaches for Spanish/Portuguese use-cases and a standard baseline for English.

Model matrix (initial candidates):
- Primary (English-first & general): Llama-2-Chat-13B (4-bit quantized) — baseline for accuracy/quality/cost tradeoff
- Multilingual candidate: BloomZ-7B1-mt (or similar multilingual instruction model) — test native multilingual capability
- Fallback / low-cost: Mistral-instruct-7B quantized — used for burst/failover and edge pools
- High-quality option (if needed): Falcon-40B-instruct for the most challenging prompts (higher cost but better factuality on some benchmarks)

Multilingual evaluation approach:
- A: Native multilingual model (BloomZ) run end-to-end
- B: Translate pipeline (Spanish/Portuguese -> English) -> Llama-2 -> translate back

Metrics to capture: accuracy/intent, slot F1, hallucination checks (automatic n-gram overlap against ground truth + manual spot checks), latency p50/p95, tokens/call (cost), and memory/KV cache efficiency.

Config notes for the POC (we'll provide an eval harness):
- Quantize candidate models to 4-bit where supported to meet latency/cost targets
- Use prefix caching for multi-turn evaluation to simulate session flows
- Run 1k labeled test prompts across English/Spanish/Portuguese slices and report per-slice metrics

I'll prepare a short Jupyter notebook and a baseline set of scripts to run the A/B comparison — Ben, will upload to the shared Drive after kickoff.

Thanks,
Aditya
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
